We need to read electron-cyclotron (EC) heating and driven current before coupling
them to transport. The [Primer](../primer.qmd) explains this source coupling;
terminology is in the [Glossary](../glossary.qmd). The selected reference writes
profiles with different averages in centimetre–gram–second (CGS) units. Their
units, radial coordinate and physical meaning must be explicit.

We added a host-side reader that preserves those distinctions. It converts units to SI,
retains the native bins and reduced-boundary flag, and hashes the exact bytes
read. Missing channels, ambiguous units, invalid grids and missing or nonfinite
values fail explicitly. Current signs are preserved.

The reader reports volume-integrated power and area-integrated toroidal current
against the corresponding reference totals. These are diagnostics: no physical
acceptance tolerance has been selected. Focused checks pass in both modes:
[24 focused tests pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-151](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-151){.cid .st-tested}. They use synthetic output files, so they establish reader
behaviour rather than reference-physics accuracy. The fixtures are constructed
separately from the reader, but are not an independent physical reference.
Installed-wheel checks also
pass in both modes; the displayed full-suite statistics remain historical.

The transport solver expects the surface average of current dotted with magnetic
field for its EC current source. The reference's current-density profiles need
an explicit field/sign and geometry conversion before coupling. Its native bins
also need mapping to the transport grid. Neither conversion is inferred here.

Two upstream ITER regression decks are prepared for the owner's baseline choice.
At this reader checkpoint, no reference execution, EC labels or training are claimed. The independent ITER
pedestal port still needs its branch and boundary prescription; M3 remains open.
The [later numerical pilot](34-genray-corrected-numerical-pilot.qmd) exercises
the reader on freshly generated reference output.
